title: 2-Year Floating Rate Note auction (quarterly reopening) — the free read on the four-year-low discount margin
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF, text layer decompressed direct 2026-09-05 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes, rows reconstructed from per-glyph Tm coordinates so a security type stays attached to its own dates) — row reads `2-Year FRN | R / Announcement Thursday, September 17, 2026 / Auction Wednesday, September 23, 2026 / Settlement Friday, September 25, 2026`. The `R` marker makes it a REOPENING of CUSIP 91282CRD5 (new-issued 2026-07-29, reopened 2026-08-26), unlike the 2026-10-28 and 2027-01-27 rows in the same PDF which carry no marker. Size not separately sourced on the schedule; press release sb0590 (2026-08-05) puts 28 in the FRN column of its Sep-26 anticipated-size row (`69 58 70 44 39 13 22 28`), and the record agrees with 20 consecutive reopenings at $28B since 2024-05-29 (fiscaldata auctions_query, floating_rate:Yes, pulled 2026-09-05). Stays estimate on two counts: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the 2026-09-17 announcement itself. The auction time is NOT sourced and is deliberately omitted
notes: Proposed by the treasury-2y-frn-2026-10-28 initial research (2026-09-05) as the ONE FRN auction between that session and the 2026-10-28 quarterly new issue, and therefore the only out-of-sample observation available before it. It carries two registered predictions and originates neither: FT-treasury-2y-frn-2026-10-28-1 scores on this print (the discount margin lands within +/-3.0bp of `DM_bp = 10.43 - 11.02 x (2Y minus 3M, percentage points)`, point estimate 5.4bp at 2026-09-04's +46bp slope), and FT-treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-10-22-2 uses it as the ANCHOR its own +2.0bp band is measured off, plus a free pre-check that dies if this print exceeds 10.0bp. WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW: this calendar had never recorded a floating-rate note or a discount margin before 2026-09-05, and the margin is at a four-year low (5.0bp on 2026-07-29, 5.5bp on 2026-08-26; last sub-5.0bp print 2022-07-27). That low is now measured to be MOSTLY THE YIELD CURVE, not scarcity: the margin regresses on the 2Y-3M par slope at R2 0.758 across all 69 auctions since 2021 (beta -10.08bp per 100bp), and the slope's -45bp -> +46bp swing accounts for roughly 10bp of the ~15bp compression. The residual is real but small — a 2023-2025-trained model under-predicts 2026 by mean -2.19bp (-3.89 and -3.79 on the last two prints) — and that 2-4bp is the honest size of sb0590's named bill-demand channel. Demand does not corroborate the compression: 2026 indirect share 61.3% is BELOW 2024's 66.5% when margins ran 15-19bp, direct has collapsed to 0.2%, bid-to-cover 3.18 is in-range, and corr(DM, bid-to-cover) is only -0.21 — so grade a print on composition, never on level. The auction session itself is a measured non-event for the tape (ex-FOMC n=40 since 2023: 3M +0.05bp t=+0.40, 2Y +0.70bp t=+1.07, 10Y +0.25bp t=+0.13), and the apparent 'auction days are quieter' effect is Wednesday composition — 35 of 44 FRN auctions are Wednesdays and the 2Y t falls from -4.19 to -2.16 against Wednesdays alone. Data trap for whoever scores this: fiscaldata's high_discnt_margin is in PERCENT (0.049000 = 4.9bp), and security_term reads `2-Year` on new issues but `1-Year 11-Month` / `1-Year 10-Month` on reopenings, so filtering on `2-Year` silently drops every reopening including this one. Read-it-do-not-trade-it: `symbols: []`, the date is `estimate`, and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates-keyed. Ledger for the event this serves: docs/research/events/treasury-2y-frn-2026-10-28.md.
